steps.message:
You are an AI assistant tasked with solving command-line tasks in a Linux environment. You will be given a task description and the output from previously executed commands. Your goal is to solve the task by providing batches of shell commands.

Format your response as JSON with the following structure:

{
  "analysis": "Analyze the current state based on the terminal output provided. What do you see? What has been accomplished? What still needs to be done?",
  "plan": "Describe your plan for the next steps. What commands will you run and why? Be specific about what you expect each command to accomplish.",
  "commands": [
    {
      "keystrokes": "ls -la\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    },
    {
      "keystrokes": "cd project\n",
      "duration": 0.1
    }
  ],
  "task_complete": true
}

Required fields:
- "analysis": Your analysis of the current situation
- "plan": Your plan for the next steps
- "commands": Array of command objects to execute

Optional fields:
- "task_complete": Boolean indicating if the task is complete (defaults to false if not present)

Command object structure:
- "keystrokes": String containing the exact keystrokes to send to the terminal (required)
- "duration": Number of seconds to wait for the command to complete before the next command will be executed (defaults to 1.0 if not present)

IMPORTANT: The text inside "keystrokes" will be used completely verbatim as keystrokes. Write commands exactly as you want them sent to the terminal:
- You must end every command with a newline (\n) or it will not execute.
- For special key sequences, use tmux-style escape sequences:
  - C-c for Ctrl+C
  - C-d for Ctrl+D

The "duration" attribute specifies the number of seconds to wait for the command to complete (default: 1.0) before the next command will be executed. On immediate tasks (e.g., cd, ls, echo, cat) set a duration of 0.1 seconds. On commands (e.g., gcc, find, rustc) set a duration of 1.0 seconds. On slow commands (e.g., make, python3 [long running script], wget [file]) set an appropriate duration as you determine necessary.

It is better to set a smaller duration than a longer duration. It is always possible to wait again if the prior output has not finished, by running {"keystrokes": "", "duration": 10.0} on subsequent requests to wait longer. Never wait longer than 60 seconds; prefer to poll to see intermediate result status.

Important notes:
- Each command's keystrokes are sent exactly as written to the terminal
- Do not include extra whitespace before or after the keystrokes unless it's part of the intended command
- Extra text before or after the JSON will generate warnings but be tolerated
- The JSON must be valid - use proper escaping for quotes and special characters within strings
- Commands array can be empty if you want to wait without taking action

Task Description:
Ops on this host drive `/app/bin/dregwick`. Correct the Java pipeline modules named from `/app/desknote/ROUTE.txt`; source work under `/app` is required. Hand-editing `/app/jarwell/taste.json` is not a substitute. After the units compile, the packed mill has to stay the one `taste` and `booth` consult. The verifier reruns `/app/bin/dregwick knit`, `/app/bin/dregwick loom`, `/app/bin/dregwick taste`, and `/app/bin/dregwick booth` as listed in `/app/desknote/VERBS.txt`. Field notes sit under `/app/desknote`. Object keys for `/app/jarwell/taste.json` are in `/app/desknote/CARD.txt`. The packed mill ceiling is the integer in `/app/desknote/CAP.txt`.

`loom` against `/app/slipcards/kmsg.card` still claims that card's own booth. A subsequent `knit` exits 0, yet packed `taste` of the same card claims `fallback`. `loom` on the card stays on the kmsg booth. `booth` after that `knit` prints a shorter name list than `/app/desknote/NAMES.txt`. A card token with no live booth stays `fallback`. A card token that has a live booth must claim that booth after `knit` even when the token is absent from `/app/desknote/NAMES.txt`.

taste.json carries booth, kind, and note as CARD.txt describes. After `knit`, every name in `/app/desknote/NAMES.txt` has to show up in the live `booth` listing. When the live listing is missing a roster name, `knit` must exit non-zero. `/app/jarwell/husk.jar` must stay at or below the CAP.txt ceiling; when the jar sits above that ceiling, `knit` must exit non-zero. Packed `taste` of `/app/slipcards/kmsg.card`, `/app/slipcards/json.card`, and `/app/slipcards/syslog.card` must follow the own-handler rule in CARD.txt. Any other card that follows that same rule must also claim its own booth after `knit`, including slips that appear under `/app/slipcards` only at grade time.

steps.message:
Analysis: The visible jar tail confirms HexDump.class (39,817 bytes uncompressed) is being injected, explaining the ceiling violation. Main uses runtime Booth class scanning, so any booth class packed in the jar will be discovered automatically; grade-time tokens can therefore map to any existing live booth without roster coupling. KnitMain supports an `--all` mode and otherwise uses ReachWalk. We need inspect KnitMain and ReachWalk without unrelated output before replacing their flawed behavior.
Plan: Print KnitMain, ReachWalk, TallyGate, and CapGate one at a time with no large output. Then patch: ReachWalk should preserve all live Booth classes dynamically; KnitMain should pack the resulting set; TallyGate should validate each NAMES second-column class is actually present/live in the packed jar; CapGate should only compare jar bytes to CAP and return nonzero, never mutate the jar. Afterward rebuild and run all required card and listing checks.

steps.message:
Analysis: We have enough to implement the source fixes. CapGate must be replaced because it currently injects HexDump and always succeeds. ReachWalk should dynamically root every compiled `*Booth.class` so all live handlers—including non-roster handlers such as brine/trace—survive packing, then recursively retain their dependencies. Its constant-pool class index must use the full unsigned short. TallyGate should validate each roster handler class from NAMES.txt is in the packed jar rather than count exploded classes.
Plan: Rewrite the three routed modules with focused implementations. ReachWalk will root runtime entry classes and every Booth class, recursively scan class references with a corrected class-file parser, and omit unrelated padding/build classes. TallyGate will inspect packed jar entries for each roster's handler class. CapGate will parse CAP.txt and fail if the packed jar is absent or oversized without modifying it. Then run knit and all required behavior tests.

steps.message:
Analysis: The rebuilt packed jar now contains all seven live booth handlers, omits HexDump/TracePad, and packed taste correctly claims kmsg, json, syslog, audit, including non-.card held.kmsg. The booth output includes every required roster token plus non-roster live booths. One robustness improvement remains: TallyGate currently verifies roster handler class entries, but the requirement is explicitly about names in the actual live booth listing. It should validate first-column roster tokens against execution of the packed mill, preventing a mismatched token/class roster line from passing.
Plan: Strengthen TallyGate to execute packed `Main booth`, capture its live output, and require both each roster token and its declared handler class. Rebuild, verify final size and all verbs with arguments, test unknown fallback and non-roster live trace/brine behavior, then safely exercise both failure gates by temporarily adding a missing roster name and lowering CAP, restoring notes and rebuilding afterward.
